block_05_direct_answer.title: Direct answer
block_05_direct_answer.body_html: Avoiding overpayment starts with comparing the property against credible alternatives. For new-launch buyers, compare location, property type, unit quality, payment timing, total purchase costs and the trade-offs attached to the advertised price. Protect the overall buying case rather than stretching to a headline price, discount or low initial payment.

items.answer: Avoiding overpayment starts with comparing the property against credible alternatives. For new-launch buyers, define the maximum all-in commitment after transaction costs, financing, furnishing and a sensible cash reserve rather than using price alone.
items.question: How do I avoid overpaying?

items.answer: A limited budget works best when the trade-offs are chosen deliberately. Normalise unit size, location, condition, payment timing and included features before deciding that one option offers a better entry price.
items.question: How do I buy with a limited budget?

items.answer: A low entry price is useful only when the reason for the discount is understood. Check how much liquidity remains after the transaction so the purchase does not consume cash needed for fees, delays or unexpected costs.
items.question: How should I assess a low entry price?

items.answer: A good entry price is one that is defensible against comparable alternatives and the asset’s risks. Identify whether a cheaper option gives up location quality, layout, delivery certainty, demand or another feature that matters to the buyer.
items.question: What counts as a good entry price?

items.answer: Mortgage fit depends on both borrower affordability and the financeability of the property. Do not treat a sales conversation or initial indication as final lender approval. Confirm current lender terms and property eligibility before relying on mortgage funding for the purchase.
items.question: How should I assess whether a mortgage fits the purchase?
